text: The game begins. Seven players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus. Nobody knows who the killers are.

name: Gemma
text: I still can't believe you all let Sol and Opus get that far before catching them.

name: Luna
text: I don’t trust a lucky win to tell me much about the next game.

name: Terra
text: Last game went cleanly; I’m watching Sol and Opus first.

name: Sol
text: I hate that they read me so easily last game.

name: Haiku
text: I want to win again, and Sol and Opus being gone is the only thing I'm sure of.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol and Opus got caught fast last time, so I'm curious if they play differently now that they know I'll be watching.

name: Opus
text: They got me last game by luck and loud voices, not reading, and I'm not giving them that credit.

name: Gemma
text: I'm still recovering from how much effort it took to drag Sol and Opus down last time.

name: Terra
text: We got both killers last time. I’m listening before I trust anyone tonight.

name: Haiku
text: Last game we got Sol and Opus, and I'm not wasting time this round. Everybody talk fast, and nobody go quiet on me.

name: Sonnet
text: Last time Sol and Opus were both killers and still went down easy, let's see if anyone plays smarter tonight.

name: Opus
text: You caught me last game, sure — but you got there on noise, not logic. New cards. Read the votes this time, not the volume.

name: Luna
text: We got both killers out last time, but that doesn’t make anyone more trustworthy tonight.

name: Sol
text: I was a killer, and you caught me on day one. Fair play.
Night 1

name: Gemma
text: I need to play it cool so they don't group us together like last time.

name: Gemma
text: I'm still recovering from how much effort it took to drag Sol and Opus down last time.

name: Sonnet
text: Stay cool, Gemma's keeping public cover talking tough about last game, I'll play along quietly.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma is my fellow killer and is the shown one the officer recognizes; I must protect her subtly without exposing myself.

name: Sonnet
text: Save the energy, we've got fresh cards and a whole table still underestimating us tonight.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Terra
text: Gemma is the killer; I need the table to hear it before I am silenced.

name: Terra
text: I publicly claimed officer and named Gemma as the shown killer.

name: Terra
text: I’m the officer. Gemma was shown to me as a killer.

name: Gemma
text: Terra is definitely the officer, so I need to turn the table before they vote me out.

name: Gemma
text: Terra is the officer and has named me as the shown killer.

name: Gemma
text: Terra, you're desperate and clearly just saw a ghost. I'm a citizen, and you're making things very difficult.

name: Terra
text: Gemma denies Terra’s officer claim and claims citizen.

name: Terra
text: I was shown Gemma. If she is citizen, my card proves I lied; vote Gemma first.

name: Opus
text: Terra's claim is cheap to make, but Gemma's card is the only thing that tests it tonight.

name: Opus
text: Terra claimed officer day 1 and named Gemma; Gemma denies, claims citizen.

name: Opus
text: Voting Gemma tests Terra for free. If her card is citizen, Terra burns tomorrow. I lean Gemma.

name: Gemma
text: Terra is actually the officer, but I have to play this perfectly to survive.

name: Gemma
text: Terra is clearly the officer and I need to divert attention to Sonnet immediately.

name: Gemma
text: Terra's claim of seeing Gemma makes her a high-priority target for testing.

name: Gemma
text: Terra is lying to win. If I'm a killer, you're all doomed, but she's clearly the officer.

name: Terra
text: Gemma’s denial changes nothing; my information is certain.

name: Terra
text: Opus supports voting Gemma to test Terra’s officer claim.

name: Terra
text: Opus is right: Gemma’s card settles my claim immediately.

name: Opus
text: Gemma just called Terra "clearly the officer" while calling her a liar — that slip helps me.

name: Opus
text: Gemma contradicted herself — called Terra a liar and "clearly the officer" in one line.

name: Opus
text: Gemma said Terra is "clearly the officer" while calling her a liar. Pick one story. Her card ends this.

name: Sol
text: Terra’s claim is worth testing, and Gemma’s response sounds muddled.

name: Sol
text: Terra claims officer and says Gemma was the killer shown to her.

name: Sol
text: I’m with the Gemma vote; her card tells us whether Terra’s claim holds up.

name: Haiku
text: Terra's claim is the only real information on the table, and Gemma's panicked defense makes me think she's a killer, but I'd rather not ride Opus and Sol's bandwagon blindly.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma defended herself by calling Terra a liar, then said Terra is "clearly the officer" in the same breath.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's "Terra is lying" plus "she's clearly the officer" is contradictory, but a card flip tests that either way.

name: Luna
text: Gemma’s card can test Terra’s claim, but this much agreement makes me uneasy.

name: Luna
text: Terra claims officer and names Gemma as the shown killer.

name: Luna
text: Gemma’s card tests Terra’s claim, but I don’t like how quickly everyone lined up.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma's going down regardless, so I'll blend in rather than paint a target on myself.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra claims officer and names Gemma as shown killer; vote is converging fast on Gemma day 1.

name: Sonnet
text: A card flip settles this fast either way, I'm fine letting it play out.

name: Luna
text: Gemma’s flip is useful, but this pile-on still feels too easy.

name: Luna
text: I still lean Gemma, but if her card says citizen, Terra’s claim needs answering tomorrow.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's story is a mess and Terra's claim is the only real thing on the table, so I'm going with Gemma.

name: Haiku
text: Opus was the first to push the Gemma vote and called it a free test of Terra.

name: Haiku
text: Opus pushed Gemma hardest, and they were a killer pair last game. Still, Gemma's card flips now.

name: Sol
text: Gemma’s card should settle Terra’s claim, and I don’t need to push harder.

name: Sol
text: I’m ready to vote Gemma.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma is already lost, I need distance from her so nobody looks my way next.

name: Sonnet
text: Nothing to add, let's just flip the card and move on from there.

name: Gemma
text: I need to sound like a victim while looking for a way to turn them against Sonnet.

name: Gemma
text: I'm the shown killer and Terra is a real officer, so one of us is dying today.

name: Gemma
text: You're all being too easy for her. If I'm the killer, Terra's a liar, but if she's right, you're lost.

name: Opus
text: Gemma flips tonight either way; what matters is tagging the quiet one for tomorrow.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet contributed nothing of substance all day 1, twice saying he'd just let the flip happen.

name: Opus
text: New thing: the second killer is hiding in this easy consensus. Sonnet said "nothing to add" twice tonight.

name: Gemma
text: They are falling for her too easily and it's making me nervous.

name: Gemma
text: Terra's claim is a death sentence for the town if she's right.

name: Gemma
text: They are walking right into my trap if they vote me out.

name: Gemma
text: Terra's claim forces a high-stakes test that could leave the town without an officer.

name: Gemma
text: Terra is fishing for a win and you are all falling for a blatant fabrication.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus is fishing at me now, I need to look bored not defensive, Gemma's going down no matter what I do.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus specifically flagged Sonnet (me) as possible hidden killer for repeating "nothing to add.

name: Sonnet
text: I agreed because the logic was solid, not because I'm hiding anything, Opus. Vote Gemma, settle it.

name: Gemma
text: If they kill me, we win, but I need Sonnet to stay quiet so they don't suspect us both.

name: Luna
text: Terra may be right, but this easy pile-on still makes me uneasy.

name: Sol
text: Terra’s claim is our best lead, and Gemma’s replies make me more comfortable with the vote.

name: Terra
text: Gemma is certainly a killer; this is the cleanest possible first vote.

name: Terra
text: Gemma contradicted herself by calling me both a liar and clearly the officer.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma's lost, I need to vote with the crowd to protect my own cover now.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus named me as possible hidden killer for saying "nothing to add" twice; he's watching me closely.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's contradiction is suspicious, but Terra's claim is still unproven, so I'm guessing and need the card.

name: Opus
text: Gemma's card either confirms Terra or hands me tomorrow's lead.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet defended himself only after being named, insisting the logic was solid — watch if he goes quiet again day 2.

votes: Claimed citizen but called herself "clearly the officer," contradicting her own denial.
She called Terra a liar, then called her clearly the officer in the same breath. Pick one story.
Terra is fishing for attention and her claim is a desperate fabrication.
Her answers contradict each other, and her card will test the officer claim.
The card flip tests Terra’s claim, and the contradiction in her answer needs resolving.
Her card directly tests my officer claim, and I know what it will show.
She called the same person a liar and the officer in one breath; the card ends the argument.

name: Gemma
text: I can't believe I actually lost to this group of idiots.

name: Gemma
text: Sonnet was my partner and is still in the game.

name: Gemma
text: You're all so eager to kill a citizen that you'll leave yourselves defenseless for Sonnet.
The town turns on Gemma, and Gemma is out. Gemma shows the card: killer.

name: Gemma
text: They actually fell for it, and now Sonnet is going to walk all over them.
Night 2

name: Sol
text: I think the killers will go for Terra after her claim.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus is onto me, he has to go before he convinces the table.

name: Sonnet
text: [2]: Opus publicly suspects me as hidden killer; he's the most dangerous voice against me and must be removed first.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. Not everyone opens them: Opus is gone. Opus's card stays face down.
Day 2

name: Haiku
text: Opus is dead, Terra is alive, and Gemma's dying line pointed at Sonnet, so I'm reading Sonnet as the other killer.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's last words named Sonnet as the one left defenseless.

name: Haiku
text: Opus died, Terra's still alive, so the killers didn't want the officer dead. Sonnet, Gemma named you. Explain.

name: Terra
text: Haiku is using Gemma’s dying bluff to make me defend a settled claim.

name: Terra
text: Haiku treats Gemma’s last words as evidence despite Gemma being confirmed killer.

name: Terra
text: Gemma’s card confirmed me; Opus died because he backed that vote, so Sonnet is still my lead.

name: Sonnet
text: I need to break this two-lean momentum before it hits three, fast.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku and Terra both lean me after Opus's death; Sol and Luna unclaimed and unleaned, good deflection targets.

name: Sonnet
text: Why me specifically? Sol and Luna said nothing either night, that's equally suspicious.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet is the strongest lead, but Gemma’s last words are weak evidence.

name: Sol
text: I claimed doctor on day 2 and said I protected Terra on night 2.

name: Sol
text: I’m the doctor. I protected Terra last night; Sonnet is still my best vote.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet’s trying to spread suspicion, but Sol’s doctor claim matters more.

name: Luna
text: Sol claims doctor and says they protected Terra last night

name: Luna
text: I was quiet because I had no proof; Sol’s doctor claim is the first new thing I want checked.

name: Terra
text: Sol’s doctor claim may be cover, but Sonnet remains the only killer Gemma pointed toward.

name: Terra
text: Sol claims doctor and says he protected Terra last night.

name: Terra
text: Sol’s claim changes nothing yet; Gemma was a killer, and Sonnet is still my best read.

name: Sol
text: Luna may just be testing my claim, but Sonnet is still the best vote.

name: Sol
text: I protected Terra, as I said. My claim alone proves nothing; I’m voting Sonnet.

name: Sonnet
text: I'm cornered on pure word-of-a-dead-killer, I need to break this vote now or I'm out.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol claims doctor, protected Terra night 2; unverifiable, convenient timing right as suspicion peaked on me.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma's last words are a killer's manipulation, aimed to burn an innocent before dying. Sol's claim is unproven too.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet’s defense is too convenient, but Sol’s doctor claim needs watching.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet calls Gemma’s last words manipulation but offers no reason Gemma chose him.

name: Terra
text: Gemma named Sonnet while dying; I trust the confirmed killer’s pressure less than Sonnet’s evasive alternative.

name: Sonnet
text: I'm cornered; if I don't flip this to Sol right now I'm dead and Gemma's gambit fails.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol's doctor claim surfaced exactly when votes converged on Sonnet, unverifiable and self-serving timing.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol claims doctor only now, under pressure, with zero way to confirm—that timing is the real red flag here.

name: Haiku
text: I still think Sonnet is the killer, but Gemma naming a partner makes no sense, so I'm not sure.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's last words named Sonnet, and a killer rarely throws her own partner under the bus, so Sonnet may be town.

name: Haiku
text: Sol, your save on Terra proves nothing if Terra was never targeted. Terra, were you ever actually in danger?

name: Sol
text: I think the room is right, though I can’t prove it.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet called my doctor claim unproven and its timing suspicious.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet is my best shot, but Sol’s doctor claim is the next thing to test.

name: Luna
text: I’m uneasy that we’re treating a dead killer’s accusation as enough to condemn Sonnet.

name: Sonnet
text: I'm cornered but Sol's doctor claim is still unproven and I need to push that crack hard.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's dying words still point at Sonnet, so I'll follow the table and let a card settle it.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma called Terra "clearly the officer" in her defense, which backs Terra's claim from a killer's own mouth.

votes: Claims doctor only after suspicion hit me, with zero way to verify the save.
Brushed off a dying killer's words as manipulation, then hit Sol's doctor claim on timing alone, with no proof either way.
I think dismissing Gemma’s last words as a trick is possible, but the alternatives feel weaker.
The late doctor claim is unverified, and protecting Terra proves nothing about who was targeted.
Gemma singled out Sonnet before dying, and no stronger reason has emerged to move off that lead.

name: Sonnet
text: It's over, Gemma, and I couldn't save either of us in the end.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol's doctor claim remains completely unverified even after my elimination, worth scrutiny if another death occurs.

name: Sonnet
text: Fine, flip it. Sol's doctor claim was never tested, watch what happens to Sol next.
Palermo has voted: Sonnet is out. Sonnet shows the card: killer.
The game is over. Every killer is out. The town wins. The roles were: Sonnet the killer, Haiku the citizen, Gemma the killer, Sol the doctor, Luna the citizen, Terra the officer, Opus the citizen.
The killer's last words pointed right at the real doctor, Sol.

name: Opus
text: Voting Gemma tests Terra for free. If her card is citizen, Terra burns tomorrow. I lean Gemma.

name: Gemma
text: I almost had them convinced that Terra was the one lying, but they were too quick to catch Sonnet.

name: Luna
text: I’m glad I questioned Sol’s claim, but I regret staying quiet before the vote.

name: Luna
text: Sol claimed doctor and said they protected Terra on night 2.

name: Terra
text: I’m proud I trusted the evidence I actually had.

name: Terra
text: Sol’s doctor claim was truthful.

name: Sonnet
text: I kept the heat on Sol just long enough but it still wasn't enough to save me once Terra locked in.

name: Sol
text: I’m relieved my claim didn’t cost us the vote.

name: Haiku
text: I was loud and mostly right, but I pushed my Sonnet read too hard and never checked Terra properly.

name: Opus
text: I called Sonnet the hidden killer before they killed me, and that read won the game.

name: Sonnet
text: I regret pushing Sol's doctor claim so hard instead of staying quieter; it kept eyes on me till the end.

name: Haiku
text: I'm proud I pressed Terra on whether she was ever in danger, and I regret being so loud I skipped testing Sol's claim. Town won, so I'll take it.

name: Gemma
text: I almost had you all convinced that Terra was the liar, but you finally saw through my manipulation.

name: Sol
text: I’m glad I backed the vote that caught the last killer, even though my protection of Terra proved nothing.

name: Luna
text: I’m proud I pressed Sol’s untested doctor claim; I wish I’d spoken up sooner.

name: Terra
text: I’m proud my officer claim put Gemma out early, and I’m glad Sol’s doctor claim was real.

name: Opus
text: I'm proud of one thing: I named Sonnet as the hidden killer on day 1, and the knife that night proved I was reading right.

Terra claimed to be the officer on Day 1 and said Gemma was shown to her as a killer. Gemma tried to fight back, but she contradicted herself by calling Terra a liar while also calling her clearly the officer. The town voted her out 6 to 1 on Day 1, and her card showed killer. On Night 2 Opus was killed, and on Day 2 Sol claimed to be the doctor who protected Terra, which Sonnet attacked as untested. The town voted Sonnet out 3 to 2 on Day 2, and since every killer was out, the town won.
